findings_addressed.documented_mutation: Remove `textwrap.dedent` call from `prepare_remote_script` in `src/intellicrack/bridges/ghidra.py` line 119; the deleted test would still pass (it only calls compile() on a string, never exercises production code), but `test_f0002_indented_call_site_does_not_leak_indentation` would FAIL because `remote_exec` would receive an indented script that `compile()` inside `_FakeBridgeClient.remote_exec` rejects with `IndentationError`, making `bridge.execute_script()` raise instead of returning `[0, 1, 4]`.

notes: G0066 was a tautological test that called only Python's built-in compile() on an indented string, verifying that Python itself raises IndentationError for indented module-scope code. This gates a Python language property, not production code. Removing textwrap.dedent from the production bridge would NOT cause this test to fail. The sibling test test_f0002_indented_call_site_does_not_leak_indentation drives GhidraBridge.execute_script() end-to-end with an identically-indented payload and asserts that (a) the result is correct ([0, 1, 4]) and (b) the script transmitted to remote_exec is dedented. That test is the real production gate for F-0002.
